Lamb Meat Cake
<note>literal: sheep cavity cake</note>
In Han Yu's poem Tuning for Zhang Ji: The female voice pours out its sincerity, demanding the wine flask be replenished. 
In Huang Tingjian's poem: Crab paste and bamboo shoots are indeed not as fine as a **Lamb Meat Cake**.

Sheep Lung
In the Ceremonies and Rituals <note>original: Yili</note>, see the entry under "Minced Pork" in the section for the Overseeing Officer.
In the Essential Arts for the People's Welfare <note>original: Qimin Yaoshu</note>, regarding the method for **Sheep Lung** stew: Take one set of lungs and boil until cooked. Cut finely. Separately make a sheep meat broth using two portions of non-glutinous rice and cook them together.

Sheep Marrow
The Comprehensive Records <note>original: Guangzhi</note> states: Melons from Liaodong, Lujiang, and Dunhuang are considered the finest. There are various names such as Raccoon Head, Honey Tube, and Dragon Hoof. The Dragon Hoof melon is as large as a bushel and comes from Liangzhou. <note>The text here appears to list "Dragon Hoof" as a type of melon rather than sheep marrow, likely due to a categorical association or textual corruption in the source.</note>

Sheep Stomach
In the Book of the Later Han <note>original: Hou Han Shu</note>, Biography of Liu Sheng-gong: See the entry under "Sheep Head."

Sheep Liver
In the Book of Wei <note>original: Wei Shu</note>, Biography of Xing Shao-yong: Shao-yong was clever from a young age and possessed great filial piety. He was especially loved by his grandfather, Shaoxian. Shaoxian had a natural fondness for **Sheep Liver**, and he would often call Shao-yong to eat it with him. When Shaoxian passed away, Shao-yong never ate **Sheep Liver** again for the rest of his life. 
In the Records of Searching for the Supernatural <note>original: Soushen Ji</note>, quoting the Ten Thousand Arts of Huainan: After a thousand years, a **Sheep Liver** transforms into a Ground Official <note>a type of spirit or toad</note>. When a toad finds a melon, it dies and becomes a quail. These are all instances where the vital energy <term>qi</term> <gloss>life force or breath</gloss> transforms and responds to create new forms.

Flowers <note>Section 217</note>

<column-break/>

In the poems of the Upper Capital, it is noted that felt houses are erected as camps. Every day the parched earth of the rooms causes the horses to be urged toward dry land. Wang Zhen’s poem states: A dream startles one daily with the dangers of past illusions and the blades of men.

**Sheep's Shoulder**
<note>original: 羊膊 yangbo</note>

In the Book of Wei, Annals of Emperor Xiaowen, it is recorded that when the Emperor was young, he was excellent at archery and possessed great physical strength. At the age of ten and some years, he was able to shatter a **sheep's shoulder** bone by flicking it with his finger. When he shot at birds or beasts, none failed to fall dead according to his aim.

Furthermore, in the Comprehensive Gazetteer of the Ming, it is noted that **Sheep's Shoulder** Mountain is located south of the city of Shazhou. It has many cliffs and rocks but no grass or trees. North of the mountain there is a cliff called Sheep's Shoulder.

**Sheep's Milk**
<note>original: 羊乳 yangru</note>

In the Compendium of Materia Medica <note>original: Bencao Gangmu</note>, under the explanation of names for the root bark of the wolfberry <note>original: digupi</note>, this term is mentioned. It is also an alternative name for the plant *Adenophora* <note>original: shashen</note>.

**Sheep's Blood**
<note>original: 羊血 yangxue</note>

In the Book of Changes, under the hexagram Gui Mei <note>The Marrying Maiden</note>, the top sixth line states: The woman holds the basket, but it contains no fruit; the gentleman stabs the **sheep**, but there is **no blood**. Nothing is favorable.

In the Commentary on the Classic of Poetry, section Si Gan, it quotes the Record of Rituals <note>Zaji</note> stating: When a temple is completed, it is consecrated with blood. The ritual involves the master of the larder wiping the sheep, lifting it onto the roof, and from the center of the roof facing south, stabbing the **sheep's blood** so it flows down the front. Then he descends. This is the ritual for consecrating a temple.

**Sheep's Fat**
<note>original: 羊脂 yangzhi</note>

In the Rites of Zhou, under the Master of the Larder, it states: In winter, one uses the fat of the owl and the feathered ones; the diet consists of fat and rank-smelling meats <note>specifically from sheep</note>. Du Zichun notes that fat and rank-smelling meat refer to the same thing.

In the Miscellaneous Records of Lu Xizhe, it mentions that the Eight Treasures of later generations are: dragon liver, phoenix marrow, rabbit fetus, carp tail, roasted owl, orangutan lips, bear paw, and crispy fried cicadas made with **sheep's fat**.

In the Record of the Splendors of the Capital, regarding the street snacks and dim sum sold at night by vendors with trays on their heads or poles on their shoulders, items include goose, pigeon, dumplings, fried cakes, and **sheep's fat** pastries.

<summary>This page catalogs historical and literary references to various parts of the sheep, including the shoulder, milk, blood, and fat. It cites diverse sources ranging from imperial histories and ritual classics to culinary records and materia medica.</summary>
<keywords>sheep, Emperor Xiaowen, Book of Wei, ritual sacrifice, Eight Treasures, Chinese medicine, culinary history, Book of Changes</keywords>

The spirit is not spirit because it is spiritual, but because of that which makes it spiritual. The sun and moon have their cycles, and the great and small have their fixed measures. Through this, the work of the sage is born and divine illumination emerges. This is the seizing of the hidden mechanism. No one in the world can see it, and no one can know it. When a superior person attains it, they strengthen their character; when a small person attains it, they treat life lightly. A blind person is skilled at hearing, and a deaf person is skilled at seeing. If one cuts off profit and focuses on a single source, the effectiveness of their efforts increases tenfold. If one reflects three times throughout the day and night, the effectiveness increases ten thousandfold.

The mind is born from external things and dies because of external things; the mechanism of this lies in the eyes. The control of birds lies in their breath. Heaven appears to have no kindness, yet from it great kindness is born. Even amidst sudden thunder and violent winds, all living things are stirred to life. Supreme joy results in a surplus of nature; supreme stillness results in a pure nature. The supreme privacy of Heaven is applied with supreme public justice. 

Life is the root of death, and death is the root of life. Kindness is born from harm, and harm is born from kindness. Therefore it is said: plunging into water or entering fire is to seek one's own destruction. Foolish people look to the vast principles of Heaven and Earth to find the sage; I look to the patterns of seasonal things. Wise people look for the sage in the worries of the foolish; I look for the sage where there are no such worries. People expect the sage to be extraordinary; I expect the sage to be ordinary.

The way of Nature is still, therefore Heaven, Earth, and the ten thousand things are born. The way of Heaven and Earth is hidden, therefore Yin and Yang prevail. As Yin and Yang push against each other, change and transformation proceed smoothly. For this reason, the sage knows that the way of Nature cannot be violated, and thus regulates it. The way of ultimate stillness is something that laws and calendars cannot fully capture. From this there are marvelous instruments, and the ten thousand manifestations are born. The Eight Trigrams and the Sexagenary Cycle <term>jiazi</term> <gloss>the sixty year calendar cycle</gloss> contain divine mechanisms and hidden spirits. The art by which Yin and Yang overcome one another is clearly displayed in these symbols.

<meta>This page continues the exploration of the "Great Void" and its relationship to the human body. The previous page discussed how the body originates from the Void; here, the text transitions into practical advice on maintaining that connection through mental clarity, dietary discipline, and the preservation of "Yang" energy.</meta>

<page-num>25</page-num>

When stillness merges with the Void, the spiritual awareness is always round and full; then, all the world’s bustle and all its burdens cannot snatch it away. If these cannot snatch it away, then the worldly heart recedes daily, and the **True Heart** <note>original: 眞心 (Zhenxin); the original, untainted state of consciousness.</note> advances daily. For every portion the worldly heart recedes, one naturally gains a portion of the True Heart. This is what the philosopher Mencius meant when he said, "**To nourish the heart, there is nothing better than lessening one’s desires.**" When the heart returns to the Great Void, the body also returns to the Great Void. As for what is called an "Immortal" or a "Buddha," why wait to discuss them further? <note>The author suggests that if you achieve this state of void-like clarity, you are already a realized being, and formal religious labels become unnecessary.</note>

Zhou Laifeng <note>A scholar or seeker contemporary to the author.</note> once asked about the techniques for **Nurturing Life** <term>Yangsheng</term>. Qian Wujiang replied:
> It is nothing more than **treading in harmony and following the natural flow**. **By treading in harmony, one is not harmed; by following the natural flow, one does not go against nature.** When one follows the breath of Heaven and Earth, reaching the pinnacle of harmony and great compliance, the human body—being a small universe—how could it not achieve the longevity of Heaven and Earth themselves?

Laifeng had these words carved in stone. At the Linqing government office, he had a small ivory tablet made and engraved these four characters—"Treading Harmony, Following Flow"—to keep in his sleeve for his entire life. Such was the weight our predecessors placed on these maxims.

**Yin and Yang are not originally opposing counterparts** <note>In this context, the author argues that Yang is the primary life force, while Yin is the vessel that holds it, rather than them being equal opposites.</note> in the creation of living things. When Yang enters Yin, and Yin retains the Yang so it cannot fly away, life is produced. When Yang leaves Yin—where the Yang disregards the Yin and cannot be stayed—death occurs. Thus, both life and death are tied to the Yang; it is truly not a matter of the Yin. The masters of the Immortal Arts say:
> **As long as one portion of Yang Breath remains, one does not die; until the last portion of Yin Breath is gone, one does not become an Immortal.**

So how can Yin and Yang be spoken of as equals? Furthermore, where the **Yang Breath** <term>Yangqi</term> resides determines not only life and death but also whether a creature is spiritually bright or dull. In humans, **Yang Breath is at the top**, which is why our ears and eyes are sharp and we are the most spiritual of all things. In birds and beasts, the Yang and Yin breaths are muddled, so they are dull. In plants, the breath is in the roots, so they are even duller. Speaking from this perspective, how can a person not treasure their Yang Breath? When the ears grow deaf and the eyes grow dim, it means the Yang is about to dissipate. This is why the superior person is cautious from the start, **guarding only the Yang**—and for good reason!

In life, one must be most careful regarding food and drink. The breath within our bodies rises, falls, gathers, or scatters because of them. Why is this?

*   **Drinking too much wine** causes the breath to rise.
*   **Drinking too much tea** causes the breath to fall.
*   **Eating too much meat or greedily consuming grains** causes the breath to stagnate.
*   **Too much spicy food** causes the breath to scatter.
*   **Too much salty food** causes the breath to sink.
*   **Too much sweet food** causes the breath to accumulate.
*   **Too much sour food** causes the breath to knot.
*   **Too much bitter food** causes the breath to be suppressed.

Those who **Cultivate the Truth** <term>Xiuzhen</term> do so by **harmonizing the five internal organs and allowing the spirit to flow**. This relies entirely on moderating the "five flavors" <note>Sweet, sour, bitter, spicy, and salty.</note> and being frugal with wine and food, ensuring nothing is in excess.

When a person first dies, their ears, eyes, mouth, nose, hands, feet, and physical form are all still there. Yet their parents, brothers, wife, and children no longer cherish them, because the spirit has departed. Thus, **what people truly love is the spirit**...

<summary>Chen Jiru emphasizes that longevity and spiritual realization come from reducing worldly desires and guarding the "Yang" energy within. He also provides a detailed guide on how different flavors in food can disrupt the body's internal "Qi" or breath.</summary>

<keywords>True Heart, Mencius, Yang Breath, Yin and Yang, Dietary Discipline, Five Flavors, Cultivating the Truth, Spirit vs. Form</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of "Nurturing Life" by Chen Jiru. The previous section established that physical health is secondary to the cultivation of "Qi" (Vital Breath) and mental stillness. Here, the author further explores the dangers of worldly competition, the necessity of emotional restraint (removing "fire"), and the philosophical origins of the human body in the "Great Void."</meta>

<page-num>134</page-num>

...[He] does not compete with the common people for profit. <note>This continues the story of the hermit Shan Bao from the previous page, who lived to seventy with the complexion of a child because he avoided worldly stress.</note> Most people worry and toil their hearts day and night without a moment's leisure; thus, old age catches up to them. Now, if one lives among the crags and drinks from the streams, they seek nothing from the world. By not sharing interest in profit with the people, one does not compete with material things. Without seeking and without competing, even if one wished *not* to live long, how could that be possible? The ancients called this **Warding off Old Age** <term>Quelao</term>. To "ward it off" simply means to remove the path that leads to aging.

There are those who love to talk about the **Way** <term>Dao</term>. I stop them, saying: "The Way is not easy to talk about. If you cannot give up lust, there is no need to talk of the Way. If you cannot withdraw from the world, there is no need to talk of the Way." Why is this? The Way is that by which we preserve our **True Self** <note>original: 眞 (Zhen); in Daoism, this refers to one's original, uncorrupted nature before it is stained by worldly experience.</note>. If one does not give up lust, the body becomes a leaking vessel; how then can the True Self be preserved? The Way is that by which we complete our **Inner Nature** <note>original: 性 (Xing)</note>. If one does not withdraw from the world, one becomes a "companion of the dust" <note>A metaphor for being entangled in the mundane and "dirty" affairs of society.</note>; how can anything be completed? 

Some might argue that abandoning one's family is not the Way, or cite the proverb that the "Great Hermit" stays in the marketplace <note>A common justification for staying in society while claiming to be spiritually detached.</note> as evidence. These are the subtle mysteries of the highest vehicle of the Zen school. If a common person uses these as an excuse, it will only lead to their own downfall and backsliding.

The **Song of Guarding Life** says:
->Water returns, but if the fire is removed, it will not turn to ash.<-
->Only if a person can remove their "fire" can they extend their life.<-

How true these words are! Human anger, envy, sorrow, intensity, agitation, rushing, jumping, dancing, singing, or even lying down and whistling—whatever is provoked by the ego—which of these is not the work of **Fire**? <note>In traditional Chinese medicine, "fire" refers to excessive emotional or physical heat that consumes the body's vital essences.</note> Wood rubbing against wood produces fire; people comparing themselves to other people produces **killing energy** <note>original: 煞 (Sha); a destructive or malevolent force.</note>. The principle is the same. If a person can break through this principle, suppressing and diminishing their ego in every matter, restraining their anger and stifling their desires, then the **Five Breaths** <note>The internal energies of the five Zang organs (heart, liver, spleen, lungs, and kidneys).</note> will naturally be level, and the **Six Pulses** will be in harmony. Longevity is then certain.

The **Ethereal and Corporeal Souls** <term>Hun and Po</term> combine to form our physical shape. Whether one is virtuous or foolish depends on their internal character; whether one is fat or thin depends on the mother; whether one is long-lived or short-lived depends on the father. When the blood is flourishing, the muscles are fat; when the **Essence** <term>Jing</term> is sufficient, the spirit is robust; when the spirit is in harmony, the character is complete. Regarding this, Wang Nongwan said: "From this we see that the mandate of heaven is bestowed; life arises from the father's essence, and death also stems from the father's essence." However, nurturing harmony and completing one's character—these depend entirely on oneself. One must not be ignorant of these tasks.

A text by **Quan Deyu** <note>A famous Tang Dynasty scholar and statesman (759–818).</note> says: 
"Boats have drownings, horses have falls, sleep has nightmares, drinking has drunkenness, eating has choking, and walking has stumbles. In extreme cases, all of these can lead to death. None are without hidden dangers." 

Alas! Does danger only reside in high offices and noble ranks? No, it resides right within food and drink, the mats and bedding, the carriages and horses, and the quiet of the bedroom. Because these are things people find "easy" and familiar, they do not guard against them. Thus, they bring danger upon themselves.

A student of the Way must realize that this body of mine comes from the **Great Void** <term>Taixu</term>. Since it comes from the Great Void, then this body originally did not exist. Why should one cling to it as a personal possession? Therefore, the **Master of Spiritual Brilliance** <note>A poetic term for the Mind or the conscious soul that "governs" the body.</note> must ensure that the heart does not cling to "being" nor cling to "non-being," just like the Great Void which has no objects to disturb it. Then, the heart of the original substance can finally attain clarity...

<summary>Chen Jiru argues that longevity is achieved by removing the "fire" of ego and competition, noting that while our physical traits are inherited, our spiritual harmony depends on ourselves. He concludes by urging the reader to view the body as a temporary manifestation of the "Great Void" to avoid worldly attachment.</summary>

<keywords>Chen Jiru, Nurturing Life, Daoism, Fire (Internal Heat), Hun and Po, Great Void, Quan Deyu, Longevity, Mental Stillness</keywords>

The great person tolerates things but does not discard things, loves things but does not indulge things. This is the Way of Heaven. Yet Heaven nourishes the myriad things with straightness; one who orders things on Heaven's behalf completes them by bending to them without harming their straightness. In this way the Way is fully realized.

<note>"Completing by bending" echoes the Great Commentary to the Book of Changes, where the sage "completes the myriad things by bending to them, leaving none out." "Nourishing with straightness" recalls Mencius's description of the flood-like <term>qi</term> <gloss>vital energy</gloss>, "nourished with straightness and not harmed."</note>

> Tolerating without discarding is the heart of completing by bending. Loving without indulging is the way of nourishing with straightness.

When the will is great, talent is great and undertakings are great; therefore it says "can be great," and also "rich possession." When the will is lasting, the <term>qi</term> <gloss>vital energy</gloss> is lasting and the virtuous nature is lasting; therefore it says "can be lasting," and also "daily renewal."

<note>All four phrases come from the Great Commentary to the Book of Changes: "Rich possession is called great undertaking; daily renewal is called abundant virtue."</note>

> Both "can be great" and "can be lasting" are rooted in the will.

Purity turns into setting oneself apart from things; harmony turns into indulging things.

> These are the ways of narrowness and of irreverence, which the noble person does not follow.

<note>Mencius judged that Bo Yi, famous for purity, was narrow, and that Liuxia Hui, famous for easy harmony, was irreverent; "the noble person follows neither."</note>

<summary>Zhang Zai describes the great person as tolerant and loving toward things without discarding or indulging them, following Heaven's way of straight nourishment. He traces greatness and endurance to the will, and warns against the extremes of aloof purity and indulgent harmony.</summary>

Xun Shuang was a man of the Later Han. Xun Shu had eight sons, whom people of the time called the Eight Dragons. The sixth was Shuang, styled Ciming. Humans and things each possess a single <term>Taiji</term> <gloss>Supreme Ultimate</gloss>; how could one say what they are endowed with is each different? It should be excised. Thus
the *Western Inscription* <note>original: "西銘" (Xi Ming by Zhang Zai)</note> states: <term>Qian</term> <gloss>Heaven</gloss> is called father, and <term>Kun</term> <gloss>Earth</gloss> is called mother. Humans dwell within their midst, following the way of sons and daughters. Therefore, Qian is Yang and Kun is Yin. The <term>qi</term> <gloss>vital force</gloss> of Heaven and Earth fills the space between the two realms, and humans and things draw upon it to form their physical substance. Qian's vigor and Kun's compliance embody the will of Heaven and Earth, serving as the commander of vital force, and humans and things attain them to form their nature. <gloss>Beneath this originally stood twenty-four characters: "This is the rectitude of decree making humanity the soul of myriad things. Other things receive it partially, stopping at merely being things." Ning</gloss>
notes: The principle of human nature and decree cannot be discussed in terms of rectitude and partiality; it is only the material endowment of <term>qi</term> that has rectitude and partiality. Now these are excised, supplementing below with the phrase "Only humanity obtains vital force that is both upright and unobstructed, hence they can extend it", yielding eleven characters in all.

<summary>This page discusses the moral endowments of animals and humans, asserting that while animals express isolated virtues, humans and things all share the Supreme Ultimate and the vital force of Heaven and Earth. The commentary critically amends earlier textual readings to clarify that innate principle is impartial, whereas only the material endowment of vital force varies in rectitude and partiality.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the text's exploration of natural anomalies as political warnings. While the previous section discussed sudden atmospheric darkening, this page focuses on geological instability and celestial rifts, interpreting them as signs of internal government corruption and the loss of royal authority.</meta>

# General Omens of Earthquakes

**A traditional Chinese landscape illustration framed within a black border. At the top of the border, the title "General Omens of Earthquakes" is inscribed. The painting depicts rocky mountains in ink and light blue/brown washes, with sparse trees and two traditional buildings with dark tiled roofs. Below the image is a block of vertical Chinese text.**

Master Zhu <note>original: "朱文公" (Zhu Wengong). Referring to the influential Neo-Confucian scholar Zhu Xi (1130–1200).</note> says: An earthquake means there is an excess of <term>Yin (the receptive or "shadow" principle associated with ministers and the earth)</term>. It signifies that ministers are usurping the ruler's power and that war will break out.

The *Annals of Song* <note>original: "宋志" (Song Zhi). Likely referring to the astronomical or "Five Elements" treatises within the official History of the Song Dynasty.</note> says: When the earth shakes, it is said that the ministers are too strong. <term>Yang (the active or "light" principle associated with the ruler and the sun)</term> is hidden and cannot emerge; *Yin* is compressed and cannot enter. This indicates an excess of *Yin*. If the maternal relatives of the emperor seize power or if the empresses and consorts interfere in government, the earth will undergo these strange changes. Likewise, if those below plot against those above or if the common people are disturbed, the earth will shake.

In terms of the broader divination, it signifies great military chaos. Regarding the seasons: in spring, the year will not be prosperous; in summer, the ruler will be filled with anxiety and the five grains <note>The five staple crops of ancient China, representing the food supply.</note> will be damaged; in autumn, war will arise; in winter, the towns will be burdened by major construction projects <note>original: "土功" (tugong). This usually refers to forced labor for walls or fortifications.</note>.

The *Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals* <note>original: "春秋傳" (Chunqiu Zhuan).</note> says: Bo Yangfu <note>A famous court official and diviner of the Western Zhou Dynasty.</note> stated: When the <term>Qi (the vital energy or life force)</term> of Heaven and Earth loses its proper order, it leads to long-term chaos. *Yang* is hidden and cannot emerge; *Yin* is compressed and cannot enter; thus, there is an earthquake.

<column-break/>

# Omens of Heaven Splitting

**A traditional Chinese landscape illustration framed within a black border. At the top of the border, the title "Omens of Heaven Splitting" is inscribed. The painting shows green and brown mountain peaks under a pale sky. A large, curved, white arc representing a rift in the sky spans across the landscape. Below the image is a block of vertical Chinese text, sparsely arranged.**

Master Zhu says: A "splitting of the sky" signifies a deficiency of *Yang*. It means the ruler is weak and the ministers are causing chaos; thus, the sky splits.

The *Annals of Song* say: A rift in the sky signifies a deficiency of *Yang*. It means the ministers are in rebellion and the ruler has lost the <term>Way (the Dao, or the moral path of righteous governance)</term>. As a result, the land itself will soon split.

Ban Gu’s *History of the Han* <note>original: "班固漢書" (Ban Gu Hanshu). An essential historical record of the Western Han Dynasty written in the 1st century AD.</note> says: A rift in the sky and a deficiency of *Yang* are both signs of subordinates becoming too powerful and prosperous, which is an omen that they will eventually harm the ruler.

<summary>This page explains that earthquakes and rifts in the sky are not merely natural disasters, but warnings of political imbalance, specifically when ministers or imperial consorts become too powerful at the expense of a weak ruler. It draws on classical historical and philosophical sources to link geological and celestial stability to the moral and administrative "Way" of the government.</summary>

<keywords>earthquake, celestial rift, Yin and Yang, Zhu Xi, political omens, Han Dynasty history, Song Dynasty history, ministerial rebellion, corruption, Bo Yangfu, Qi, the Dao</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the text's exploration of natural phenomena as political omens. Having established the "substance of Heaven" and "form of the Earth" on the previous page, the author now provides specific divinations for atmospheric and geological anomalies, citing authorities like Zhu Xi and historical annals to link these events to foreign invasions and internal political corruption.</meta>

# Divination on Sudden Changes in the Sky

**A landscape illustration depicting rugged mountain peaks and trees under an ominous, dark grey sky. The heavy clouds suggest a sudden atmospheric change, reflecting the subject of the divination title above.**

Master Zhu <note>original: "朱文公" (Zhu Wengong). Referring to the great Neo-Confucian philosopher Zhu Xi.</note> says: If the color of the sky suddenly changes, the surrounding tribes <note>original: "四夷" (Siyi). Historically translated as the "Four Barbarians," referring to non-Han peoples surrounding the Chinese heartland.</note> will come to invade.

The *Annals of Song* <note>original: "宋志" (Song Zhi). Likely referring to the astronomical or "Five Elements" treatises within the official History of the Song Dynasty.</note> says: A sudden change in the sky’s color is called the "Black Constant" <note>original: "黑常" (Heichang). A technical term for an unnatural, persistent darkening of the sky viewed as a dire omen.</note>. It signifies that the surrounding tribes will come to invade.

The *Great Plan* <note>original: "洪範" (Hong Fan). A classic text from the *Book of Documents* which correlates human behavior with natural phenomena.</note> says: Clarity and brightness are the essential substance of Heaven. A sudden change in the sky’s color is called the "Black Constant."

<column-break/>

# Divination on Sudden Sinking of the Earth

**A landscape painting showing green-peaked mountains and a valley with two small buildings. The ground in the foreground near the houses is depicted with dark lines indicating cracks or subsidence, visually representing the "sinking earth" omen.**

Master Zhu says: If the earth suddenly sinks, the myriad people will be scattered and dispersed.

The *Annals of Song* says: When the earth sinks, it means subordinate officials are monopolizing power. The myriad people will be scattered; it also signifies the loss of territory.

Jing Fang <note>A Han dynasty scholar (77–37 BCE) famous for his system of interpreting the *I Ching* to predict disasters.</note> says: If a mountain sinks of its own accord without cause, military conflict will arise throughout the world.

Fan Ye’s <note>The historian (398–445 CE) who compiled the *Book of the Later Han*.</note> *Book of Han* says: The sinking of the earth signifies that the royal house is in chaos and high ministers are monopolizing governance.

### Technical Vocabulary

**Sinking Earth** <note>original: "地陷" (Dixian). Geological subsidence interpreted as a sign of collapsing social or political stability.</note>
**Sky Color** <note>original: "天色" (Tianse). The appearance of the heavens, which was monitored for signs of the "Will of Heaven."</note>
**Master Zhu** <note>Zhu Xi, whose philosophy integrated natural observation with moral governance.</note>
**Annals of Song** <note>An official dynastic history used as a reference for historical omens.</note>
**Jing Fang** <note>An expert in Yi Jing (Book of Changes) divination and astronomical omens.</note>
**Fan Ye** <note>The primary author of the *Book of the Later Han*.</note>
**Book of Han** <note>An official history covering the Han Dynasty, often cited for its records of strange portents.</note>
**The Great Plan** <note>A foundational text of Chinese political philosophy and cosmology.</note>
**Monopolizing Power** <note>original: "專政" (Zhuanzheng). An official or minister ruling without the Emperor’s consent.</note>
**Scattered and Dispersed** <note>original: "離散" (Lisan). The displacement of the population, usually due to war or famine.</note>
**Military Conflict** <note>original: "兵作" (Bingzuo). Literally "the rising of weapons" or the start of a war.</note>
**Surrounding Tribes** <note>The "Four Barbarians" of the cardinal directions.</note>
**Black Constant** <note>A specific atmospheric phenomenon signaling impending doom.</note>

<summary>This page lists divinations regarding sudden atmospheric and geological changes, interpreting them as omens of foreign invasion and domestic political corruption. It draws on authorities like Zhu Xi and the Book of Han to warn that natural disasters reflect a breakdown in the ruler's authority.</summary>
<keywords>divination, omens, Zhu Xi, Jing Fang, political corruption, foreign invasion, Black Constant, sinking earth</keywords>

### Chronic Fright Induced by Vomiting and Diarrhea in Children

When vomiting and diarrhea in young children develop into <term>manjing</term> <gloss>chronic fright wind, characterized by lethargy, exhaustion, and mild convulsions</gloss>, the child falls into a drowsy stupor, and the hands and feet twitch faintly without severe spasming. Take half an <term>liang</term> <gloss>a traditional Chinese ounce, about 15 to 20 grams</gloss> of <term>Jinye Dan</term> <gloss>Golden Liquid Elixir, an alchemical sulfur-based preparation</gloss> and three <term>qian</term> <gloss>a traditional measure, about 3 to 4 grams</gloss> of <term>Bai Wanzi</term> <gloss>White Pills, a phlegm-clearing pediatric formula containing arisaema and aconite</gloss>. Grind them together extremely fine, and administer the powder mixed in ginger-infused rice water. Taking up to three <term>qian</term> or more will bring effectiveness, and taking up to one or two <term>liang</term> will cause no harm. Once the <term>weiqi</term> <gloss>stomach qi, the digestive and vital energy</gloss> is revived, the hands and feet will gradually warm up, and the dosages should be tapered down: gradually reduce the Golden Liquid Elixir and increase the White Pills, adjusting the proportions according to clinical judgment.

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of the Yuddhajayarnava, where Shiva explains the calculation of "Chashakas" (tiny units of time) to the Goddess. While the previous page established the elemental associations of the planets, this page focuses on the practical application of these cycles in divination (Prashna) and the vital importance of the "breath" (Prana) in determining success or failure.</meta>

### Page 3

#### Su. Ja. Na. 3

The rule is remembered thus; in this way, one should understand the five <term>chashakas; a unit of time measuring 24 seconds, or 1/60th of a ghatika</term>. Currently, there are twenty-seven *chashakas* <note>The number 27 likely correlates to the 27 Nakshatras or lunar mansions</note> for the Rule of the Sun above. Thus, half and half, in the twenty-seven half-*chashakas*.

<margin>Su. Ja. Na. 3</margin> <insert>In the same way</insert> In this very manner, the measure for the Moon and the other leading planets is declared by these *chashakas*. The Wind <note>the element Vayu</note> moves sideways; in an inquiry <term>prashna; a branch of astrology where a chart is cast for the moment a question is asked</term>, the "Life-glance" <note>original: "jiva-drik"; a specific favorable planetary aspect or internal state</note> is remembered. In the burning <note>the fire element</note>, actions are destroyed, O Dear One. When moving through the middle <note>the central channel or sushumna</note>, being in the middle grants great happiness. In the water element, a middle union is considered to increase growth and lifespan.

The prescribed action should be performed by these five <note>the five elements or five time-units</note>. For entering or departing, or in the union of actions, the Wind is auspicious. In war, for victory, and in pleasure, the Wind is very beautiful <note>very favorable</note>. When moving in the equinox <term>vishuva-chara; referring to the balanced flow between the nostrils or the central path</term>, O Goddess, the result is declared to be mediocre.

Having understood this, the wise man should perform actions as he desires. Whether the breath is in the left, the right, or the middle, one should declare the good or bad results, O Dear One. Where the portion of the Breaths <term>prana; the vital life-force or the flow of breath in the nostrils</term> is found, there the inquiry will bring good fortune. In the opposite case, the reverse happens and the action will be destroyed.

Regarding going or not going, the "Foot of the Breath" <term>pranapada; a specific mathematical point in a horoscope related to the breath</term> provides the answer. Success is achieved when the breath has reached the "foot"; it is not achieved when it has moved to the fruit-less side. In an auspicious union of wealth, the Moon will be in Virgo. Whether in an inquiry or at the moment of birth, this is the truth, the truth, O Excellent One.

<meta>This page continues the secret teachings of the Yuddhajayarnava, transitioning from the internal state of the warrior to the external cosmic forces. Shiva begins to map out how the planets, elements, and directions interact to create the "fivefold time" that determines success or failure.</meta>

<gloss>Of these three</gloss>

The nectar of speech is obtained through internal reflections; in this fivefold time, among such people, a person of such radiance is rare. Therefore, I have not shown a full elaboration here, but rather a brief overview <term>dig-darshana; literally "a showing of the directions," meaning a summary or guiding outline</term>. Fire is above, water is below, and the Wind <term>prabhañjana; "the breaker," a poetic name for the wind god Vayu</term> moves sideways. In the middle is the void of space. Within this fivefold system, the Sun, the one who is only a head <note>Rahu, the demon of the ascending lunar node</note>, the Son of the Earth <note>Mars</note>, and the Slow-mover <note>Saturn</note>—these rise toward the south. They are cruel planets <term>krura; malefic planets that bring harsh or difficult results</term> and perform cruel actions. The Teacher of the Immortals <note>Jupiter</note>, the Teacher of the Asuras <note>Venus</note>, the Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note>, and the Night-maker <note>the Moon</note> rise on the left; they perform both auspicious and inauspicious actions. The Sun is fire; the Lame One <note>Saturn</note> is earth; water is... <note>OCR here is fragmented</note> ...this is the rising of the planets, <insert>O Dear one</insert>. The Moon is water; Venus is fire; the Teacher of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note> is wind. The Earth and the Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note> rise with a leftward movement, O Dear one. Situated in their own state, between the left and right paths, are two *ghatikas* <note>a unit of time lasting 24 minutes</note> and thirty... <unclear>caṣāstriṃśat</unclear>. This practice is considered separately. The time for a change would be half of that, and half of that again... or even for the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>. For the Moon, it is half; for the Son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note>, half; and for Mercury and Jupiter, a half of a half. Thus in this fourfold group, the fourfold...

<summary>Shiva explains the elemental and directional associations of the planets, categorizing them into "cruel" (malefic) and "auspicious" (benefic) groups based on their movement and elemental nature. He provides specific time measurements for their influence, emphasizing that this knowledge is a rare "overview" of cosmic laws.</summary>
<keywords>astrology, planets, five elements, malefic planets, benefic planets, Rahu, Saturn, Jupiter, Venus, ghatika, Yuddhajayarnava</keywords>

<meta>This page transitions from the astrological timing (Muhurta) discussed on the previous page to the study of internal energy channels (nadis) and physiognomy—the reading of physical signs on the body, particularly for women. The numbering jumps from the previous page's section 11 to section 54, suggesting a thematic shift within the manuscript.</meta>

### The Assembly of Channels and Vital Breath

...In the state of exhalation <term>recaka</term> <note>the specific yogic practice of controlled breathing out</note>, the assembly of channels <term>nāḍī</term> <note>subtle conduits in the body through which life-force flows</note> is established. **54**

The channels flow through the body's currents without remainder. They pulsate from other channels and are thus produced in the shape of a serpent <note>original: *sarpa-ākāra*; a common description for the winding path of subtle energy or Kundalini</note>. Among them, the multitude of channels is governed by the single vital breath <term>prāṇa</term> <note>the primary life-force</note>, which resides in the intellect of the wise. **55**

By mastering the breath, one's self becomes like a jewel. [Through this mastery], the blood is purified. 

<margin>Varpa</margin> <note>Original: *Varpa*; this may be a proper name or a specific technical term for a type of energy</note> Know that by binding the collection of rays, one attains the higher worlds. <margin>58</margin> <note>The number 58 is written in the margin, corresponding to the page number</note> **56**

### Rules of Form and Physical Signs

Through the rules of bodily form <term>mūrtividhāna</term> <note>the science of interpreting physical features to predict character or destiny</note>, one finds wealth and prosperity. Even if certain signs are diminished, if she possesses a son, happiness, and a beloved, and follows the traditional rites, she will live a long life. Good character, virtue, and conduct [are indicated]. However, if [malefic signs] are present in the body, it leads to the loss of wealth and the wasting of the frame, whether in men or in women <term>yoṣitāṃ</term>. **57**

A memory of the vital breath brings a wealth of resources. It is certain that she will have a daughter and a son. It is destined that she shall have no co-wife <term>sapatnī</term> <note>original: *sapatnī*; a second wife sharing the husband, historically a sign of domestic competition or misfortune</note> to contend with. She will find pleasure in her husband and remain dedicated to the performance of higher duties <term>dharma</term>, and her authority shall not diminish...

<insert>
When the signs are found in a pair, she remains stable in the home. Auspicious signs such as the mirror and the blue lotus <note>original: *ādarśotpala*; symbols of beauty, clarity, and divinity</note> [bring] strength and... **58**
</insert>

<summary>This page describes the "serpent-shaped" subtle channels (nadis) and their connection to the breath (prana), before shifting into physiognomy to predict a woman's lifespan, children, and domestic status.</summary>
<keywords>nadi, prana, recaka, physiognomy, sapatni, women's signs, vital breath, dharma</keywords>

units.prev_translation:
<meta>This page continues the technical discourse on Muhurta (auspicious timing) for religious ceremonies, specifically marriage. It follows the previous discussion on calculating planetary "piercings" and now introduces the concept of *Latta* (planetary "kicks") and the duration of ill-omens before a time becomes pure again for rituals.</meta>

...[struck] by the planetary "kick" <term>latta</term>. <note>original: *latta*; a specific astrological affliction where a planet "kicks" or affects a lunar mansion (nakshatra) at a certain distance.</note> Afterward, seven or nine <note>referring to specific time units or counts of nakshatras</note> **10**

When Rahu <note>the north node of the moon, often called the "shadow planet"</note> or Venus <note>original: *sita*</note> are in the fifth or twentieth positions, they should be avoided. The Moon <note>original: *uḍupa*</note> strikes the person’s form, but no other planet does so. **10**

A time is considered inauspicious <note>original: *naiṣṭaṃ*</note> when it is joined with malefic planets <term>krūra</term> <note>planets like Saturn, Mars, or the Sun</note>, when a planet moves toward a malefic, when it is aspected by the Sun, or when it is pierced by a malefic. Furthermore, if the time is corrupted by portents <term>utpāta</term> occurring in the sky or atmosphere, or if it is affected by a malefic planetary "kick" <term>latta</term>— **11**

<margin>pro[ceeding] <unclear>k</unclear></margin> <note>The marginal note "pra ka" likely refers to *prakaraṇa*, indicating a specific section or chapter reference.</note>

—or if there is a "war" between malefic planets <note>a planetary war or *yuddha* occurs when two planets are at very close longitudinal proximity</note>, or it is corrupted by the three types of portents, or falls within the inauspicious time of *Vishti* <note>a specific division of the day considered unlucky for starting new works</note>, no auspicious ceremonies <term>maṅgaleṣu</term> should be performed. Only after the disturbances of meteors <note>original: *ulkā*</note> or thunderbolts <note>original: *aśani*</note> have passed, and the experts deem the time to be clear <note>original: *nirmala*</note>, should one proceed for an auspicious purpose. **12**

In the ritual of "taking the hand" <term>pāṇigrahe</term> <note>referring to the marriage ceremony</note>, the relationship of the sixth and eighth houses <note>original: *ṣaṣṭhāṣṭake*; a configuration known as Shashtashtaka, usually considered highly unfavorable as it signifies enmity or death</note> leads to death or loss of children. A relationship of the ninth and fifth houses <note>original: *nava-pañcame*</note> results in friendship, while the second and twelfth positions <note>original: *dhana-dvādaśake*</note> affect wealth and expenditure. However, love may still exist between the couple if the lords of their signs are the same. **13**

If the lord of the bride’s sign <note>original: *bhuvanapati*</note> is a friend of the groom's, or if they share the same planetary ruler, then even with other afflictions, the marriage can be auspicious. This is especially true if there is purity of the stars <term>tārā-viśuddhau</term> <note>a calculation based on the couple's birth stars to ensure compatibility</note> for the groom. **14**

<summary>This page details astrological prohibitions for marriage, focusing on malefic planetary "kicks" (Latta), the duration of bad omens like meteors, and the compatibility (Kuta) between the bride and groom's birth signs.</summary>
<keywords>Latta, Rahu, Malefic planets (Krura), Auspicious rituals (Mangala), Meteors (Ulka), Marriage (Panigraha), Stellar purity (Tara-vishuddhi), Muhurta</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of Swarodaya (the science of phonetic and breath divination). While the previous page established general time-units and general vowel mappings, this page introduces the specific "Wheels" (Chakras) used to calculate the relationship between a person’s name, the planets, and the zodiac signs.</meta>

### || The Wheel of Letters and Vowels ||
| A | I | U | E |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| ka | kha | ga | gha |
| ca | cha | ja | jha |
| ṭa | ṭha | ḍa | ḍha |
| ta | tha | da | dha |
| pa | pha | ba | bha |
| ma | ya | ra | la |
| va | śa | ṣa | sa |
| ha | | | |

<note>original: "Varnasvaracakram"; This table maps the consonants of the Sanskrit alphabet to four primary vowels to determine phonetic resonance.</note>

### || The Wheel of Planets and Vowels ||
| Ja <note>likely representing the Sun or a specific phonetic group</note> | A | I | U | E | O |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ca** | Aries | Ka <note>syllable</note> | Sagittarius | Nu <note>syllable</note> | Ma <note>syllable</note> |
| **Ṭha** | Leo | Mi <note>syllable</note> | Pisces | Taurus | Aquarius |
| **Da** | Taurus | Ka <note>syllable</note> | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **Ba** | Sun | Moon | Jupiter | Venus | Saturn |
| **Ra** | Mars | Mercury | : <note>aspiration/visarga</note> | : | : |

<note>original: "Grahasvaracakram"; This table correlates vowels with the twelve zodiac signs (Rashis) and the seven traditional planets.</note>

### || The Wheel of the Life-Vowel ||
| A | I | U | E | O |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Group A | Group Va | Group Ka | Group Ca | Group Ṭa |
| 1 | 6 | 5 | 5 | 5 |
| Group Ta | Group Pa | Group Ya | Group Śa | Group Kṣa |
| 5 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 4 |

<note>original: "Jivasvaracakram"; This system is used to identify the "Life-Vowel" (Jiva-svara) which represents the living essence of an individual's name.</note>

Regarding the sixteen syllables... **|| 1 ||** From the groups of letters beginning with 'A', we determine the life-vowel from the name **Devadatta** <note>a traditional placeholder name, like "John Doe"</note> as an example: The letter 'Da' has the value of 3; the vowel 'I' above 'Da' has the value 11; the letter 'Va' followed by 'U' has the value 1; 'Va' itself has the value 4; the 'Ta' following 'Da' has the value 1; the letter 'Da' has the value 3; the joined letter 'La' in the sequence has the value 2; the vowel 'A' has the value 1. The total sum is twenty-six (26). When divided by five, the remainder is one (1). Therefore, for Devadatta, the <term>Life-Vowel; the primary phonetic frequency governing a person's life-force</term> is 'A'. **|| 2 ||** Thus ends the Wheel of the Life-Vowel. 

### || Now, The Wheel of the Zodiac ||

The sixteen groups of syllables are formed from the letters starting with 'Ka' and the five groups ending in 'La'. When four letters are combined, the group number is declared. The group of 'A' and the group of 'La' represent the pure name. **|| 1 ||** In a name, the vowel and the first letter are known as the phonetic markers. These are divided by five, and the remainder is known as the Life-Vowel. **|| 2 ||** Thus ends the section on the Life-Vowel. 

For the vowels 'A' and 'I', there are nine <term>Navamshas; a "ninth-part" or sub-division of a zodiac sign used for precision</term> of Aries, nine of Taurus, and six of Gemini, totaling twenty-four. With three more divisions of Gemini, there are the signs of Cancer and Leo, totaling twenty-one. For the vowel 'U', there are nine divisions of Virgo and nine of Libra. Along with three divisions of Scorpio, these total twenty-one. For the vowel 'E', there are six divisions of Scorpio, and nine each for Sagittarius and Capricorn, totaling twenty-one. For the vowel 'O', there are three remaining divisions of Capricorn and eighteen divisions for Aquarius and Pisces, totaling twenty-one. Thus is the "Vowel-Sign" described, following the sequence of the <term>Navamsha; the sub-divisional chart</term>. **|| 3 ||** Thus ends the Wheel of Zodiac Vowels.

<note>original: "Rashisvaracakram"</note>

Regarding the explanation of the <term>Nakshatra-carana; the "feet" or quarters of the lunar mansions</term>: The vowel 'A' is the ruler of the quarters of the lunar mansions starting from Ashvini through Mula. For the five mansions following Punarvasu, including the 'Ni' sound and the quarter-divisions, the vowel 'I' is the ruler. For Uttaraphalguni, including the 'Ni' sound and the four mansions starting from Hasta, plus two quarters of Anuradha, the vowel 'U' is the ruler. For the remaining two quarters of Anuradha, the four mansions starting from Jyeshtha, and three quarters of Shravana (totaling twenty-one quarters), the vowel 'E' is the ruler. For the final quarter of Shravana and the mansions starting from Dhanishtha to the end (totaling twenty-nine quarters), the vowel 'O' is the ruler. In the name Devadatta, the vowel is 'A' and the sign-vowel is also 'A'. **|| 3 ||** Thus ends the Wheel of the Zodiac.

<summary>This page details three diagnostic "Wheels" (chakras) that map phonetic sounds to planets, zodiac signs, and life-forces, providing a mathematical formula using the name "Devadatta" to identify an individual's primary astrological vowel.</summary>
<keywords>Varnasvaracakram, Grahasvaracakram, Jivasvaracakram, Rashicakram, Navamsha, Life-Vowel, zodiac divisions, Devadatta, phonetic astrology</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of Swarodaya (the science of phonetic and breath divination). It transitions from general vowel-measurements to specific time-units called Narodaya and provides a detailed mapping of Sanskrit vowels to the twelve signs of the zodiac (Rashis) and their planetary rulers.</meta>

<margin>

</margin>

Regarding the "dead vowels" <note>original: "mṛtasvarā"; sounds that have lost their potency in a specific divinatory context</note>... **|| 15 ||** Now, the time-measurements for the twelve-year cycle of the <term>Narodaya; literally 'the arising of man,' a calculation used to determine the timing of events based on the sounds of a name</term> are explained. In the period of *Shaka Pushya* <note>a historical or astrological timeframe</note>... **|| 16 ||** Regarding the essence of the nectar... **|| 17 ||** Regarding the "Gaja-Pranagi" <note>a technical term for a specific rhythmic or astrological measure</note>... **|| 18 ||** 

The measures for the twelve-year cycle of Narodaya are 11 | 7 | 8 | 98 <note>these represent specific units: Ghatikas, Palas, and their subdivisions</note>. The annual Narodaya measure is also 11 | 7 | 8 | 98. The measure for the <term>Ayana; the six-month solar progression (solstice)</term> is 7 | 0 | 58 | 09. The measure for the transit is 7 | 23 | 56 | 3. The monthly Narodaya measure in <term>Palas; a unit of time equal to 24 seconds</term> is 1 | 18 | 71. The general Narodaya measure is 7 | 49 | 03. The daily Narodaya measure is 7 | 32 | 8. The hourly <term>Ghatika; a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</term> Narodaya measure is 39. Thus ends the section on the eighteen measures. Now, the importance of the vowel-measures is explained:

In the time of desire... **|| 20 ||** Regarding the sound of the vowels... **|| 21 ||** One should establish the sound of the vowels. **|| 21 ||** Through the syllables: Aries, Leo, and Scorpio <note>original: "meṣa-siṃhāli"; 'Ali' refers to Scorpio</note>. The sound **A** corresponds to Aries, Leo, and Scorpio. These syllables/signs are the forms of the vowels. Whichever vowel corresponds to a sign, the lord of that sign is also the lord of that vowel. For example, the vowel **A** takes the form of Aries, Leo, and Scorpio. The lord of Aries and Scorpio is Mars <note>original: "Bhīma"</note>; the lord of Leo is the Sun <note>original: "Sūrya"</note>.

---

The "dead vowels" are the short sounds... like the star Revati. From that, a youth becomes powerful; a youth who is not red is powerful. **|| 15 ||** In the Shaka [era] or the month of Pushya... twelve and more. The Indra-cycles are seven [3?], according to the standard. **|| 16 ||** Measure 98... Likewise, the measure for the solstice in Palas is "Elephant-Arrows" <note>a mnemonic for the number 58</note>. Fire, barley, and arrows... fire, eyes, and units of Palas. **|| 17 ||** The "form of the elephant" is described as the measure for the month... Nine, full, nine-eyes, six, and parts of the measure. **|| 18 ||** The measure of the asterism (Nakshatra) comes from fire, according to the sequence of the day. Through the measure of the <term>Ghatika; 24-minute unit</term>, the Narodaya vowel is found. **|| 19 ||** <term>Now, the Planetary Vowels</term>: The vowel **A** belongs to Aries, Leo, and Scorpio. The vowel **I** belongs to Virgo, Gemini, and Cancer. The vowel **U** belongs to Sagittarius and Pisces. The vowel **E** belongs to Libra and Taurus. **|| 20 ||** The vowel **O** belongs to Capricorn and Aquarius. Mercury, Venus, the Friend [Sun], Mars, and Jupiter are the lords of Aries and the others in sequence. **|| 22 ||** 

->**|| Thus ends the Wheel of Planetary Vowels ||**<-

---

Mars and the Sun are the lords of the [A-vowel] syllables. Likewise, for Virgo and Gemini, the lord is Mercury; for Cancer, the Moon. Therefore, Mercury and the Moon are the lords of the **I** vowel. For Sagittarius and Pisces, the lord is Jupiter; thus Jupiter is the ruler of the **U** vowel. For Taurus and Libra, the lord is Venus, the ruler of the **E** vowel. For Capricorn and Aquarius, the lord is Saturn; Saturn is the lord of the **O** vowel. 

Now, an example is given: <gloss>The fourth quarter of the star Revati.</gloss> For the syllable **Re** in the star Revati: The star Revati corresponds to the sign of Pisces. The vowel in Revati is **E** <note>the text here explores the phonetic components</note>. Pisces is represented by the **U** vowel. The lord of Pisces is Jupiter, who is the lord of the **U** vowel. Therefore, for a person named Devadatta, the vowel is **U**. Likewise, for the word beginning with **Ya**: The phonetic power is found in the star Jyeshtha. In the word "Yajña," the letter **Ya** corresponds to the star Jyeshtha and the sign of Scorpio. Scorpio's lord is Mars. Therefore, for the word "Yajña," the planetary vowel is **A**.

->**|| Thus ends the Wheel of Planetary Vowels ||**<-

<header>Chapter Six</header>

### Chapter Six

> A definitive judgment in this matter arises from the instructions of a Guru <note>spiritual teacher or expert guide</note> and through numerous practical examinations. || 42 ||

> If the sum of the longitudes of the Ascendant, Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, Gulika <note>a mathematical point representing the son of Saturn, often malefic</note>, the Moon, and the Sun coincides with the birth asterisms <note>the Nakshatras of the querent</note>; or if they fall in the "destruction" asterism <note>the 2nd, 7th, or 88th division</note>, the "fatal" asterism, or the asterism of Revati <note>the final constellation of the zodiac</note>, then death or great calamity will occur immediately. || 43 ||

> The degree of the Ascendant is known as the "Body" <note>Vapu</note>, that of the Moon as "Life" <note>Prana</note>, and that of Gulika as "Death" <note>Mrityu</note>. If these points are devoid of mutual conjunction or aspect, but are aspected by their respective lords, one should predict a long and firm life. If there is a conjunction or aspect between the "Body" and "Death" points, there will be physical pain and disease; if between "Life" and "Death," it causes delusion or unconsciousness for the querent. || 44 ||

> If the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika fall in dual signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note>, they bestow death and disease. If they fall in fixed signs, they are neutral; if in movable signs, they grant long life and health to the querent.

**Regarding "Lagna..." ||** The "sum of the Ascendant etc." refers to the <term>Pancha-Sphuta</term> <note>the "Five-fold Longitude" calculated by adding five specific points</note>. The <term>Vainashika</term> <note>the "Destructive" point</note> refers to the 88th quarter-division of the zodiac. The <term>Paushna-bha</term> <note>the "Star of Pushan"</note> refers specifically to the Revati constellation. || 43 ||

**Regarding "Lagnasya..." ||** This connects the degrees of the Moon and Gulika. By the word "their," the conjunction with the Death-point is implied. "Of that life" refers to the vital breath. One must also examine the relationship of these points to the "angles" <note>Kendras</note> and other houses. By multiplying the longitudes of the Ascendant, Moon, and Gulika by nine, one should respectively derive the <term>Prana, Deha, and Mrityu Sphutas</term> <note>the calculated points for Life-force, the Physical Body, and Death</note>. || 44 ||

**Regarding "Dvandvamsha..." ||** <term>Dvandvamsha</term> refers to the Navamsha <note>ninth-part division</note> of a dual sign; it implies the previously calculated Life, Body, and Death points are situated in signs associated with dissolution. If they are in mutual trines <note>120 degrees apart</note>, it means they share a <term>Trikona</term> relationship. <unclear>That word...</unclear>

<summary>This page details the calculation of sensitive astrological points—Body, Life, and Death—and explains how their placement in specific constellations or zodiacal divisions predicts health, longevity, or imminent demise.</summary>
<keywords>Pancha-Sphuta, Gulika, Prana-Deha-Mrityu, Revati, Vainashika, Navamsha, longevity, medical astrology</keywords>

वसवोष्टौ । मुनयः सप्त । जनिभमुपगते मृत्याविति शेषः । सार्पपौष्णेन्द्रभे स्थित इति

<meta>This page continues the technical discussion of astrological calculations used to predict the outcome of illness or the timing of death, specifically focusing on the 'Trishphuta' (Triple Sensitive Point).</meta>

<page-num>24</page-num>
<header>The Path of Inquiry</header>

->Those planets associated with the Triple Sensitive Point and the stars of danger<-
->bring harm to the querent;<-
->while benefics located in the angles and other houses bring good results.<-
->This is the supreme secret. || 40 ||<-

->Multiply the elapsed minutes of the degree occupied by the Triple Sensitive Point<-
->by nine, and divide by the fixed number (twenty-seven).<-
->Count the remainder from the star of the Triple Sensitive Point;<-
->the resulting star is the Star of Death.<-
->The star occupied by the Quadruple Sensitive Point is also considered thus.<-
->If the illness of the querent should subside,<-
->then the Quadruple Sensitive Point will affect a relative<-
->born under that specific star. || 41 ||<-

->When the Moon reaches the sign occupied by the Triple Sensitive Point,<-
->death occurs for the patient.<-

<note>The "Triple Sensitive Point" (Trishphuta) is a calculated longitude combining the positions of the Ascendant, the Moon, and Gulika (a mathematical point representing Saturn's son).</note> By the term <term>stars of danger</term><note>original: "vipat-pratyara-vadha-nakshatras"</note>, we refer to the 3rd, 5th, and 7th stars from the birth star. The order is changed here to highlight that the "Star of Destruction" (the 7th) carries the greatest defect, while the "Obstacle Star" (the 5th) is less severe. They "bring harm" during their respective major or minor planetary periods. Similarly, benefics "bring good." This is the "supreme secret," meaning it is the essential core of the teaching and should only be taught to students who have been well-tested. || 40 ||

**Regarding the verse "Those..."**: Of this degree. <term>Multiplied by nine</term><note>original: "dhighna"</note>. <term>By the fixed number</term>, meaning twenty-seven. Divide and count the remainder starting from the star occupied by the Triple Sensitive Point. The star arrived at is the <term>Star of Death</term><note>original: "Mrityubham"</note>. Death of the querent may occur when a planet transits that star. Furthermore, the <term>Quadruple Sensitive Point</term><note>the Trishphuta plus the position of the Sun</note> and the star it occupies is also a Star of Death. Some say the Star of Death should be known from the ninth-division (Navamsha) of the Quadruple Sensitive Point, just as with the Triple Point. That should also be considered for the sake of consistency. If there is "subsidence of illness," meaning the querent recovers, then the Quadruple Sensitive Point "enters a relative," meaning the misfortune transfers to a kinsman of the querent born under that star. 

The procedure is as follows: Set down the Triple Sensitive Point, multiply by nine, discard the signs, double the degrees, multiply those and the minutes by nine, and divide by twenty-seven. The remaining number of degrees should be used for counting from the Triple Point's star. Note this detail: if there are remaining minutes, the next whole number after the degree count should be taken. This determination of the time of death is necessary only when the Triple Sensitive Point indicates the presence of a fatal defect. || 41 ||

**Regarding the verse "In the Triple..."**: Another method for determining the timing is stated by this. || 42 ||

<summary>This page details the mathematical calculation of the 'Star of Death' using the Triple and Quadruple Sensitive Points to predict a patient's fate. It explains how astrological afflictions may either result in the querent's death or transfer to a relative if the querent recovers.</summary>
<keywords>Trishphuta, Star of Death, Quadruple Sensitive Point, Prashnamarga, Vedic astrology, medical astrology, Nakshatra, calculation of death</keywords>

**In the Haṭhayogapradīpikā**

# **Root: Through practice, one should draw the vital fluid falling into the woman's vagina upwards.**
# **Even if one's own vital fluid has been discharged, one should draw it upwards and preserve it. || 87 ||**

->॥ COMMENTARY ॥<-

**Action.** Having commissioned a smooth probe <note>original: *śalākā* — a rod or catheter</note> made of lead <note>original: *sīsaka* — historically used for medical instruments, though toxic by modern standards</note>, suitable for insertion into the male organ <note>original: *meḍhra*</note> and measuring fourteen finger-widths <note>term: <term>aṅgula</term> — a traditional unit of measurement roughly equal to the width of a finger</note> in length, one should practice its insertion into the organ. On the first day, one should insert it to the depth of one finger-width. On the second day, two finger-widths. On the third day, three finger-widths. In this gradual manner, when the insertion reaches twelve finger-widths, the urethral passage becomes purified. 

Then, one should have a similar probe made, fourteen finger-widths long, but with a one-finger-width curve at the tip, facing upwards. One should insert this twelve finger-widths deep, leaving the two-finger-width curved, upward-facing portion outside. Then, taking a tube similar to a goldsmith's blowpipe <note>original: *agnidhamana-sādhani-bhūta-nāla*</note>, one should insert its tip into the curved, upward-facing two-finger portion of the tube already inside the organ and perform a blowing action. By this, the passage is thoroughly purified. 

After that, one should practice drawing up water through the male organ. Once the drawing of water is mastered, one should practice drawing the vital fluid <note>term: <term>bindu</term> — literally "drop" or "point," referring here to the essence of life-force or semen</note> upwards according to the method described in the previous verse. When the drawing up of the vital fluid is perfected, the success of **Vajrolī Mudrā** is achieved. This is only accomplished by one who has conquered their breath <note>original: *jitaprāṇa*</note> and no one else. It becomes fully effective when both **Khecarī Mudrā** <note>term: <term>Khecarī Mudrā</term> — a practice involving the tongue being turned back into the nasal cavity</note> and the mastery of breath are attained. || 86 ||

As such, when the practice of Vajrolī is mastered, the author describes the subsequent practice: **In the woman's vagina...**

->॥ VERNACULAR EXPLANATION ॥<-

Having done this, one should practice entering it into the organ. On the first day, insert it one finger-width. On the second day, insert two finger-widths. On the third day, insert three finger-widths. In this gradual way, when it reaches twelve finger-widths, the passage of the organ is purified. That fourteen-finger probe should be made such that two finger-widths are curved with the opening facing upwards. Then, insert twelve finger-widths inside and keep the two-finger-width curved, upward-facing opening on the outside. After that, take a tube like the one a goldsmith uses to blow on a fire. Place the front of that tube into the middle of the two-finger-width curved opening of the probe that was inserted into the organ, and then blow. By doing this, the passage of the organ is thoroughly purified. 

Following this, one should practice pulling water upwards through the organ. When the attraction <note>original: *ākarṣaṇa* — suction or drawing in</note> of water begins to happen properly, then, using the method described in the previous verse, one should practice the attraction of the vital fluid. When the attraction and drawing in of the vital fluid is mastered, then **Vajrolī Mudrā** is perfected. To whomever **Khecarī Mudrā** and the conquest of breath are both mastered, to that person **Vajrolī Mudrā** will be successful, and not to anyone else. || 86 ||

When the practice of **Vajrolī Mudrā** is thus perfected, the further means are described: **In the woman...**

> यावद्बिंदुः स्थिरो देहे तावत्कालभयं कुतः ॥ ८९ ॥

## ॥ टीका ॥

नौ पततीति पतन् पतंश्चासौ बिंदुश्च पतद्बिंदुस्तं पतद्बिंदुं रतिकाले पतंतं बिंदुमभ्यासेन वज्रोलीमुद्राभ्यासेनोर्ध्वमुपर्याहरेदाकर्षयेत् । पतनात्पूर्वमेव । यदि पतनात्पूर्व बिंदुराकर्षणं न स्यात्तर्हि पतितमाकर्षयेदित्याह ॥ चलितं चेति ॥ चलितं नारीभंगे पतितं निजं स्वकीयं बिंदुं चकाराद्रजः ऊर्ध्वमुपर्याकृष्याहृत्य रक्षयेत् स्थापयेत्॥८७॥

वज्रोलीगुणानाह ॥ एवमिति ॥ एवमुक्तरीत्या बिंदुं यः संरक्षयेत् सम्यक् रक्षयेत् स योगविद्योगाभिज्ञो मृत्युं जयत्यभिभवति । यतो बिंदुः शुक्रस्य पातेन पतनेन मरणं भवति । बिंदोर्धारणं बिंदुधारणं तस्माद्बिंदुधारणाज्जीवनं भवति । तस्माद्बिंदुं संरक्षयेदित्यर्थः ॥ ८८ ॥

सुगंध इति ॥ योगिनो वज्रोल्यभ्यासिनो देहे बिंदोः शुक्रस्य धारणं बिंदुधारणं तस्मात्सुगंधः शोभनो गंधो जायते प्रादुर्भवति । देहे यावद्बिंदुः स्थिरस्तावत्कालभयं मृत्युभयं कुतः । न कुतोऽपीत्यर्थः ॥ ८९ ॥

## ॥ भाषा ॥

भगे इति ॥ रतिकालमें स्त्रीकी योनिमें जानै पड्यो और पडे नही जा पहलै जो बिंदु नाम वीर्य ताय वज्रोलीके अभ्यासकरकें ऊपरि आकर्षण करे जो पडे पहलै बिंदुको आकर्षण न होय तो नारीके भगमें गिरपड्यो जो अपनो बिंदु ताय और स्त्रीको जो रज ताकूंबी ऊपर खेचकर स्थापन करे ॥ ८७ ॥

अब वज्रोलीके गुण कहें हैं ॥ एवमिति ॥ या रीतकर जो बिंदुं कूं स्थिर करे सो योगवेत्ता होय हे. और वो मृत्यु कूं जय करे. और बिंदुजो वीर्य ताके पतनकरकें तो मरण होय हे. और जो वीर्यकूं यारीतसूं धारण करे तातें जीवन होय हे. तातें बिंदु कूं या रीतकर स्थित करे ॥ ८८ ॥

सुगंध इति ॥ वज्रोलीके अभ्यास करवेबालेके देहमें वीर्यके धारणतें बोहोत सुंदर सुगंध प्रगट होय हे. और जबतांई बिंदु स्थिर रहे तबतांई कालको भय नहीं होय ॥ ८९ ॥

<meta>This page continues the transition from Viparītakaraṇī Mudrā into the specific technical instructions and requirements for Vajrolī Mudrā. The previous page established that Vajrolī is a powerful practice that can be mastered even by those who do not follow all the strict rules of Yoga, provided they have access to specific aids like milk and a partner.</meta>

( 109 )
### Third Instruction

**Root Verse: One should gradually practice the proper upward contraction of the genitals. Whether a man or even a woman, one may attain success in Vajrolī. || 85 ||**

**Root Verse: With effort, using a proper tube, one should perform a blowing action into the "Vajra-cave" <note>original: "Vajrakandare" — referring to the urethral opening</note>. This should be done slowly and gradually to facilitate the circulation of air. || 86 ||**

---

->॥ COMMENTARY ॥<-

**I shall speak** or describe. What are the two things which are difficult to obtain for just anyone, or for someone without means? They are either "hard to acquire" or "impossible to acquire." This is supported by the dictionary <note>original: *kośa*</note> definition that the prefix *duḥ* signifies difficulty or prohibition. 

In response to the question "What are those two things?", the text says: **Milk**. One thing is milk for drinking. After using the organ, because of the resulting weakness of the senses, drinking milk is appropriate to regain strength. Some practitioners say milk is for suction <note>original: *ākarṣaṇa*</note> during the practice itself, but that is incorrect; if the milk were to thicken or curdle inside, it would be impossible to expel. The second thing is a woman who is submissive and under one's own control. || 84 ||

The method of **Vajrolī Mudrā** <note>term: <term>Vajrolī Mudrā</term> — an advanced Hatha Yoga practice involving the control and sublimation of sexual energy and fluids</note> is now described. **By the organ...** Following union with a woman, using the discharge of the **Bindu** <note>term: <term>Bindu</term> — literally "drop," referring to the vital seed or semen, considered the essence of life force</note> as the means of the practice, a man or even a woman should practice the gradual and correct upward contraction through effort. By contracting the genitals and drawing the seed upward, one may attain success in Vajrolī Mudrā. || 85 ||

Now the preliminary process of Vajrolī is described. **With effort...** With a "proper tube," meaning a tube made of lead <note>original: *sīsaka*</note> or similar materials, one should perform a blowing action <note>original: *phutkāra*</note> slowly and gradually, much like one blows through a pipe to kindle a fire. This blowing into the **Vajra-cave** (<note>original: <term>Vajrakandara</term></note>), the opening of the urethra, is done to ensure the circulation of air moves properly through the channel. Therefore, one should perform this repeatedly and with great care. Now, regarding the means of practicing Vajrolī...

---

->॥ VERNACULAR EXPOSITION ॥<-

First, one should drink milk because after union with a woman, the senses become weak; therefore, drinking milk is necessary. The second thing is an obedient and submissive woman. || 84 ||

Now the method of Vajrolī Mudrā is stated. **By the organ...** After union with a woman, when the "drop" falls, the man or even the woman should practice contracting the organ upward with effort. By pulling the vital seed back up, success in Vajrolī Mudrā is obtained. || 85 ||

Now the preliminary action of Vajrolī is stated. **With effort...** Using a tube made of silver <note>original: *chāndi*</note>, one should blow into the opening of the organ slowly, just as one blows to light a fire, so that air circulates. This should be done repeatedly. Now the process of practice is stated: a probe <note>original: *śalākā*</note> should be made of lead, four finger-widths long, which is smooth and suitable for entering the organ...

<summary>This page details the physical requirements for Vajrolī Mudrā, including the use of milk for physical recovery and the technical method of using a tube (made of lead or silver) to blow air into the urethra to prepare the channel for the upward suction of vital fluids.</summary>
<keywords>Vajroli Mudra, Bindu, sexual sublimation, Hatha Yoga, Yoga anatomy, Shastranala, Phutkara, Brahmacharya</keywords>

### Eight-petaled, very radiant,
### with filaments and a pericarp. ॥ 56 ॥

One should <term>samāropya</term> <gloss>place or visualize</gloss> the <term>kanda</term> <gloss>root-bulb</gloss>, which is the source of the lotus. Through the technique of pressing the "scent of the rutting elephant" <note>a technical yogic practice involving the contraction of the perineum or lower abdomen to stimulate the energy center</note>, one should raise the bulb in the region of the <term>nābhi</term> <gloss>navel</gloss>. The <term>nāla</term> <gloss>stalk</gloss> is described as being twelve inches long because it represents the nature of the <term>prāṇa-śakti</term> <gloss>vital life force</gloss> and spans the distance between the navel and the heart. ॥ 55 ॥

The text now describes its pervasiveness:

### The bulb there is composed of power;
### on the stalk, indeed, are thorns.
### These are the worlds
### of the Rudras, O beautiful one. ॥ 57 ॥

### The knot should be composed of Maya,
### situated in the impure path.
### The lotus of knowledge is very radiant,
### adorned with the pericarp and seeds. ॥ 58 ॥

After the invocation:

### With perfumes, incense, and flowers,
### and various types of food and drink,
### one should worship the God of the gods of gods,
### fashioned solely in the mind. ॥ 54 ॥

And thus:

### Having meditated on the self as Bhairava,
### one should then perform the sacrifice in the heart.

This sequence is begun in order to turn even the subtle body <term>puryṣṭaka-śarīra</term> <gloss>the "city of eight" consisting of the five elements and the inner organs</gloss> into the nature of Bhairava. ॥ 54 ॥

Now, the text describes in detail the implantation of the "seat" <term>āsana</term> for the self, who is the object of worship and of the nature of Bhairava:

### Having placed the bulb in the navel,
### and a stalk twelve inches long, ॥ 55 ॥

### reaching as far as the heart—
### there, one should contemplate a lotus.

<summary>The practitioner is taught to perform an internal mental worship of the self as Bhairava. This includes visualizing a lotus growing from a bulb at the navel up to the heart to serve as a ritual seat for the deity.</summary>

—is restricted by a clear object, and that state of the principle of consciousness <term>saṃvit-tattva</term> is called "knowledge" <term>jñāna</term>. When the object is unclear and involves the mind, it is "intention" <term>saṅkalpa</term>. When it reaches the stage of being an object for the intellect, it is "determination" <term>adhyavasāya</term> or "certainty." This separateness of the object and the internal/external senses is inconsistent with the non-difference of their light; yet, it is made to appear by the principle of consciousness <note>the impure subject</note>. Because this resting place is in "difference"—unlike the states of <term>Īśvara</term> or <term>Sadāśiva</term> where difference rests in non-difference—knowledge, intention, and so on are described as separate powers of the one synthesizing principle of consciousness whose own nature remains un-destroyed. In this way, the variety of things like "blue," as well as doubt and other states, are all held together in an unbroken unity. [Verse 18]

Now, one might object: Let the nature of the power of consciousness as "reflection" be granted in the case of intention, memory, and so on, which are conceptual <term>savikalpa</term>. But what about the power of direct experience <term>anubhava-śakti</term>, which is characterized by immediate perception and is non-conceptual <term>nirvikalpa</term>? Reflection <term>pratyavamarśa</term> is—

---

<note>403. "By the principle of consciousness" refers to the impure subject <term>aśuddha-pramātṛ</term>.</note>
<note>404. Even though the status of the object is restricted in a living being governed by the life-force and the subtle body <term>puryaṣṭaka</term>, it is still eternal because it resides within the Supreme Self.</note>
<note>405. "Unbroken" <term>akhaṇḍitam</term> means non-different.</note>
<note>406. This refers to "the nature of reflection."</note>

<summary>The text distinguishes between knowledge, intention, and determination based on the clarity of the object and the faculty used. It then introduces an objection: can direct, non-conceptual perception truly be called "reflection"?</summary>
